approval_required_for: Any proposed change to the board-facing memory layout, address map, stream ordering, transfer/beat protocol, or major runtime/interface assumption.

executable_actions.on_failure: Record each unresolved or contradictory fact with its source and affected constraint; do not claim a checker pass, infer board-specific values, or promote the audit as board/runtime readiness. Route major layout or protocol changes for approval before adopting them.
executable_actions.rationale: Extract a traceable board-facing contract from the supplied detailed profile and evidence, preserving unknowns rather than guessing. Run the designated static checkers against the resulting data-order, transfer, memory, and runtime records before they are consumed in SACG planning.

observations: state_summary lists target_board_profile, field_evidence, field_evidence_candidates, and case_adapter as input artifacts. The candidate-stage summary exposes only selected keys and abbreviated structures, not their substantive board facts; this is a detail-visibility limitation, not evidence that the artifact classes are absent.

No board-specific data order, tensor dimension order, byte order, lane packing, element width, transfer count, AXI data width, beat interpretation, burst behavior, or ready/valid/liveness contract can be verified from the visible contents.

No DDR capacity or usable region, base addresses, address map, alignment, buffer ownership/lifetime, initialization mechanism, runtime ABI, or weight/image-loading facts are exposed in the supplied summary. These remain unconfirmed rather than established absences.
No checker results are supplied for memory_runtime_plan_check, stream_plan_check, addr_map_check, or sacg_static_check; this audit does not claim those checks passed.
The visible SACG memory truth reports zero active contamination barriers and zero open retry or backtrack requests. No current SACG-memory blocker is indicated.

Later contracts should cover only the Transformer-block accelerator boundary; do not extend DUT memory or weight-consumption requirements to embedding/tokenization, final model norm, LM head/logits, or sampling.
proposed_actions: Have the next preparation pass inspect the detailed target_board_profile, field_evidence, and case_adapter payloads and record each board-facing fact with its source, or mark it unresolved when the detailed evidence does not document it.

Produce explicit data-order/transfer and memory/runtime audit artifacts, then run the four role-appropriate static checkers. Keep checker outcomes and evidence bindings explicit; do not mark undocumented facts as satisfied.
Escalate for approval before any later proposal that changes the board memory layout, address map, stream/beat protocol, or other major architecture/interface assumption.
risks: Without detailed board facts, deriving beat counts, tensor-to-byte mappings, address ranges, or runtime buffer requirements would require guessing and could create inconsistent stream, memory, and deployment constraints.

Once full inputs are available, cross-check model shapes and numeric element widths against tensor ordering, packing, transfer counts, AXI beat width, alignment, and memory-map capacity; the supplied view cannot establish consistency.
A missing or ambiguous board protocol or memory-layout fact must remain unresolved for SACG extraction; do not silently substitute a generic DDR/AXI wrapper or inferred board convention.

edges: target_board_profile and field_evidence -> documented board data-order and transfer contract
target_board_profile and field_evidence -> board memory, address-map, DDR/AXI, and runtime constraints
model/shape/numeric policy -> tensor layout, packing, and transfer-count assumptions (values require detailed artifacts)
documented contracts -> stream_plan_check, memory_runtime_plan_check, addr_map_check, and sacg_static_check

Board-specific ordering, beat, memory-map, DDR/AXI, and runtime facts therefore cannot be confirmed or called missing. Handoff these details for checker-backed extraction before SACG planning; no board or runtime readiness is claimed.
